2P-proc · benchmark branch · validation report

Non-rigid z-correction on real recordings

The stimulus-locked artifact in Scnn1aAi14_D1M2 / 08292026 / run1 is reproduced in Python, explained as axial brain motion, and used to benchmark how the F_anat movie should be built and applied. Results replicate across four mice, both extraction backends and two stimulus types.

Written for the Wang lab 2P group (Vincent, Manuel). Data: D1M2 run1/run2, B1M0 04182024 run1, B2M0 04192024 run3, A2M0 12152023 run1. Env: validation/pixi.toml (CaImAn 1.12.2, Suite2p 0.14.0).

Summary

The artifact is z-motionAfter 67.5 mJ laser stimuli the brain moves ~1.6 planes (µm) at 1.45 s and again at ~2.4 s. Each ROI's spurious excitation or suppression has the sign and size predicted by F_anat (r = 0.58 across ROIs).
Non-rigid F_anat works; rigid does notThe MATLAB non-rigid subtraction removes most of the artifact in every session. A global zpos regression barely helps and removes 15–18% of real signal.
Per-patch, per-frame depth is essentialUsing one depth for the whole field, or a fixed per-patch tilt, leaves the artifact almost intact. Smoothing patch depths over time or space also hurts.
Two refinements help strong casesSkipping the 3-frame movmean of F_anat and assigning soft (sub-plane) depths remove the residual left on D1M2 run1 (trial z-dependence +0.17 → −0.02). On weaker artifacts all F_anat methods already reach ~0.

1 · Reproducing the example figures

The MATLAB analysis (analyze_2p_with_Beh_func.m, steps 1–6 and 11–12, 'F' / 'raw' path) is ported in validation/stim_response_analysis.py: piecewise-linear ΔF/F baseline fitted on pre-stimulus frames, F_cell_anat as the uniform ROI-pixel mean of the 3-frame-smoothed F_anat, per-ROI OLS slope over all frames, bad-ROI rejection (F0 < 70, R² > 0.25, max SNR < 6, noise level > 10) and rastermap ordering. With the iscell labels Manuel shared, the port keeps 539 / 499 ROIs (without / with subtraction) against 535 / 495 in the MATLAB figures.

Why the earlier real-data tests showed no effect

The previous tests used C57_O1M2 / 10022023, a recording without trials, and judged whole traces. The z-artifact that matters here is locked to the stimulus and lasts 2–4 frames; it only becomes visible, and measurable, in trial averages. All metrics below are built around the trial structure.

2 · Mechanism

3 · How the methods are scored

No real recording has ground truth, so each metric targets one failure mode without assuming the answer. All variants are compared on one fixed ROI set per session (ROIs kept without z-correction), so the R² rejection cannot favour any of them.

  • Held-out trial-wise z-dependence (main metric). The z-model is fitted on even trials only. On odd trials, after removing per-stimulus means, the dff step at the z-jump frame is correlated across trials with the F_anat step, for the 25% most z-loaded ROIs. 0 means no z left; negative means overcorrection.
  • z-locked residual. Across-ROI correlation between the trial-averaged residual and the F_anat prediction in the z-jump window.
  • Injected signal kept (ground truth). Synthetic GCaMP responses (3 SD, τ = 0.3 s) are added to 30% of real ROIs, starting at the z-jump, with amplitude proportional to each trial's z-step (the worst case: real activity coupled to the motion). The fraction of the injected trial-average that survives correction is reported; 1 means nothing was removed.
  • Also computed: spontaneous z-jump triggered deflections, physiologically impossible frame-to-frame drops, and significance counts (section 5).

F_anat construction

The production F_anat picks, per frame and per 60 × 60 px patch, the z-stack plane (within zpos ± 5) with the highest Gaussian-smoothed R², and averages overlapping patches. Each ROI's F_anat trace can be written as a sum of per-patch contributions, so any depth-selection rule can be evaluated exactly in seconds (validation/fanat_variants.py; the production rule reproduces the production F_anat to r = 0.99999994).

60 px patches (~87 µm) are best. A denser grid of the same patches (stride 24) reduces the argmax residual by about a third at 2.2× the compute; with soft depth the grid density stops mattering.

5 · What changes for the biology

Significantly excited / suppressed ROIs in the z-jump window (1.35–1.6 s vs the last 0.5 s of baseline, Wilcoxon over trials of the strongest stimulus, Bonferroni p < 0.01):

Without correction, D1M2 run1 shows 11 (Suite2p) or 6 (CNMF) significantly "suppressed" cells at the z-jump; all F_anat corrections remove them. Counts in the late window (2–3 s) barely change. These counts have no ground truth; the injection test is the check that real responses survive.

6 · Issues found along the way

  • Stimulus labels on D1M2 run1. params_matlab.json uses the template rand_stim_seq, but Bruker delivered 175 ms instead of 225 ms at block position 11 (trials 11, 31, 51, 71, 91). Five of the twenty "67.5 mJ" trials were 52.5 mJ. The older sessions match the template exactly. params_from_bruker() builds the trial vector from the VoltageOutput files.
  • Behaviour videos. The BehaviorCam*_t2.mp4 files in the run1 folder are run2's (30 trials × 4 s × 200 Hz = 24,000 frames). The run1 videos (_t1) are needed to reproduce the wipe-trial selection.
  • ΔF/F scale. Detection is identical to Manuel's run (same 3051 ROIs), but ΔF/F is ~5× smaller here, so the F offset of the movie given to Suite2p differs (here negative values are clipped at 0 when writing mcorr_movie.tiff). The comparison is unaffected; absolute ΔF/F values depend on this choice.
  • R² rejection. MATLAB rejects ROIs whose z-model explains R² > 0.25. A better z-model raises R², so the rejection removes more ROIs (668 → 631 on D1M2 run1). It may be better to judge ROIs on the corrected trace.
  • zstack_shifted.tif is written into the raw ZSeries folder; in production that is the source data directory.

7 · Pipeline changes on the benchmark branch

  • F_anat out-of-memory fix (compute_zcorr.compose_f_anat_non_rigid). The old composite stored a z-stack crop per patch and frame; on 8000 frames at 765 px it was killed at 190 GB. The new version builds each pixel from the z-stack directly: identical output (0 differing pixels), 59 GB peak.
  • CNMF export fix (extraction.prepare_cnmf_object). With the template's p = 0, CaImAn 1.12.2 crashes in select_components; the scalar g is now cleared first.
  • Opt-in fast / soft F_anat (compute_zcorr.f_anat_non_rigid_fast), enabled by a z_motion_correction.f_anat block, e.g. {"depth_mode": "soft", "beta": 200, "half_window": 8}. With the defaults (argmax, ±5) it reproduces the production F_anat exactly. Without the block nothing changes.

8 · Recommendations and what is implemented

Pipeline changes are on the 2P-proc benchmark branch. MATLAB changes are on a local branch zcorr_recommendations of Analysis_2P_Manu (off dev_manu, not pushed).

  1. Keep non-rigid F_anat subtraction; avoid rigid zpos. MATLAB now warns when subtract_z = 'rigid'.
  2. No movmean on F_anat. It is never worse on the held-out metric and keeps more signal. Default off in run_roi_zcorr (roi_correction.f_anat_smoothing = 1) and in MATLAB (params.zcorr.f_anat_movmean = 1). MATLAB now caches the unsmoothed F_cell_anat_raw.mat; a legacy smoothed F_cell_anat.mat is used with a warning.
  3. Soft depth, with an auto mode. roi_correction.depth_mode = "auto" builds the per-ROI F_anat traces for argmax and soft depth (β = 400, 200, 100) from patch_depth_profiles.npz, and keeps the rule that best predicts held-out fluorescence steps at z-events (cross-validated over time blocks, on the z-loaded ROIs; soft must beat argmax with p < 0.01). It needs no trial structure. On all six sessions it selects soft depth, with p < 1e-5 in every one: as a predictive model of z-artifacts, soft depth is better even where the trial metrics could not tell the methods apart. The small negative trial z-dependence of soft depth on weak sessions (−0.03) is measured against argmax-based z-steps, so it does not by itself show overcorrection. MATLAB uses the pipeline's F_cell_anat_rois.mat (Suite2p, iscell rows) when present. Default stays argmax.
  4. Trial labels from Bruker. The pipeline writes stim_sequence.json (per-cycle VoltageOutput waveforms and frame counts) at concatenation. MATLAB check_stim_sequence.m warns on mismatches and relabels when params.general.use_bruker_stim_sequence is true. Tested in Octave: it reports trials 11, 31, 51, 71, 91 on D1M2 run1.
  5. R² rejection is configurable (params.analysis_post_stim.max_R2_z, default 0.25 unchanged).

Also changed: the vectorised F_anat path is now the default (identical output, verified end-to-end on run2) and saves the patch depth profiles; run_roi_zcorr read CNMF ROI pixels in C order instead of CaImAn's Fortran order, now fixed.
